newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, January 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, January 10.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Former President Francesco Cossiga said the set up of a bi-cameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms should be approved by a referendum. National Alliance party leader Gianfranco Fini backed the proposal, while Pds leader Massimo D'Alema said "It's a joke" (all).
* The Popular party, a moderate movement supporting the ruling coalition, opened its annual congress in Rome in search of a new leader, as secretary general Gerardo Bianco is resigning (all).

* The cabinet will discuss today a draft reform of Italy judicial system put forward by Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick which would allow plea bargaining for all crimes where the maximum sentence is three years (all).

* The Constitutional Court cleared a controversial new law on parties financing, approved by Parliament in December. The law allows citizens to fund political parties with a contribution from their income tax declaration (all).
* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers's association Confindustria, said the government should not wait until March to push through a supplementary mini-budget cutting public spending (all).
* Confindustria backed engineering employers association Federmeccanica'reject of the government proposal to end a long-running row on metalworkers contract (all).
* In an interview Eu Commissioner Mario Monti says Italy is still halfway on the road to join Emu and "it is late to be just halfaway" (Corriere della Sera).

* The Milan stock exchange roared ahead, buoyed by strong domestic buying which drove up banks and insurance companies. The blue chip index ended up with a 3.93 percent gain. The lira hit a new high against the mark at 974.50, the best level since June 1994 (all).

* Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani met Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of white goods company Zanussi, who joined force with US comapny Centenary to bid for information technology group Olivetti's ailing pc division (Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
